28: Here [one is talking about the issue of] Damages - where he would be obligated to pay the compensation if he did not kill him but only caused him damage. For when it comes to damages there is no difference whether it was caused inadvertently  or intentionally, or whether it was done with a downward or upward motion, as we expound in Bava Kamma (26b) [when the verse says] "A laceration for a laceration" [this comes to teach us] that one is obligated for inadvertent damages as [he would be] for intentional damages, and for damages caused beyond his control as [he would be] if they we done willfully.
